Bilgoraj New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Biłgoraj, Poland

Not demolished. This is the third of Biłgoraj's Jewish cemeteries, established around 1800, a companion to the Old (second) cemetery documented elsewhere in this collection. The Germans carried out mass executions here during WWII, burying victims in mass graves that remain unmarked and unlocated; in 1948, a group of Jews returned to exhume and rebury additional victims from around the town. In 1985–86, part of the site was fenced and a Holocaust memorial and lapidarium erected, and in 2015 a further memorial, the 'Wall of Remembrance,' was added. Over 200 matzevot survive today, the oldest dated 1826.
